max_tire.size: ≈32 in (e.g. 255/70R18; 275/65R17 with a slight liner rub)
max_tire.note: Consensus from owners of the twin Lexus GX 460, which shares the body and suspension. Test-fit on a Prado, whose bumpers differ by grade.
GX 460 owners report it needs upper control arms, the right offset, a body-mount chop, liner removal and pinch-weld work.

tsbs.title: Manual DPF regeneration switch
tsbs.summary: Standard across the 1GD/2GD Prado, HiLux and Fortuner range from June 2018 as a DPF countermeasure.

tsbs.title: DPF exhaust hardware and software remedy
tsbs.summary: Toyota's free-of-charge repair for affected 2.8 and 2.4 diesels, combining revised exhaust hardware and software.

timeline.change: J150 launches in Japan on 14 September and in Australia on 16 November. Debut of KDSS with an electric accumulator, Crawl Control, Multi-Terrain Select and the Multi-Terrain Monitor
Unsealed 4X4 flags launch-year trucks for airbag recalls and electrical gremlins
April: left-hand-drive Prados included in Toyota's VSC software recall after the Lexus GX 460 'Don't Buy' episode
Australian Altitude grade added between GXL and VX
First facelift (Japan 10 Sept, Australia October): new grille, bumpers and lamps, LED low beams, retuned suspension, five-mode MTS. Three-door dropped in Australia
June: 1GD-FTV 2.8 diesel (130 kW / 450 Nm) replaces the 1KD-FTV 3.0. AC60F six-speed auto. DPF arrives. V6 dropped in Japan
Diesels sold October 2015 to April 2020 covered by the Australian DPF class action
Second facelift on 12 September. V6 dropped in Australia. Unsealed 4X4 flags 2017 trucks for head-unit, ESC-light and shift glitches
June: manual DPF regeneration switch standard
August update: 150 kW / 500 Nm, 3,000 kg braked towing, auto only, 9-inch screen with CarPlay and Android Auto
Production ends in October; replaced by the J250

identify.intro: The 150 was sold under several names and with several engines, and its US twin wears a Lexus badge. The model code tells you what you're looking at.

items.head: Model codes
items.body: KDJ150/155 = 1KD-FTV 3.0 diesel. GDJ150 = 1GD-FTV 2.8 diesel. TRJ150/152 = 2TR-FE 2.7 petrol. GRJ150 = 1GR-FE 4.0 V6. GRJ152 = 3.5 V6 (China). URJ150 = Lexus GX 460. A 155 suffix is the short three-door.

items.head: Market names
items.body: In the UK the J150 was sold as the Land Cruiser LC3, LC4 and LC5 by equipment level. Australian grades were GX, GXL, Altitude (from 2012), VX and Kakadu, plus the three-door SX and ZR until 2013.

items.head: Facelift tells
items.body: 2013-on trucks have the larger grille and new lamps. 2017-on trucks have the second face with the vertical-bar grille. 2020-on Australian trucks have the 9-inch CarPlay screen.

items.head: DPF countermeasures
items.body: On a 2015–2020 diesel, look for the manual DPF regeneration switch (standard from June 2018) and ask a Toyota dealer whether the 2020 remedy is recorded against the VIN.

items.head: Spare and sub-tank
items.body: Trucks with the spare on the tailgate keep the 63-litre sub-tank. Under-floor spare versions give it up.

paragraphs: Toyota never sold the Prado 150 in the US. Americans got the Lexus GX 460 instead. NHTSA lets vehicles at least 25 years old be imported without meeting federal standards, and the first 150s were built in late 2009, so they don't become eligible until late 2034.
Until then, a US buyer who wants a J150 should buy a GX 460. Many Prado-specific parts, from the front end to bumpers, have been fitted to GXs by owners on IH8MUD.

production.intro: The 150 ran for fourteen years and was built in Japan, China and Russia.
